items.title: CSR and financial performance — the evidence is mixed but tilts positive
items.claim: Friede, Busch and Bassen's 2015 meta-analysis aggregated over 2,000 studies on the link between ESG (environmental, social, governance) factors and corporate financial performance. What did it find?

options.text: ESG and financial performance are negatively related across the board
Around 90% of studies found a non-negative relationship; the majority showed positive correlation between ESG performance and financial performance, though magnitudes are modest
No study has examined this question
ESG is required to be at least cost-neutral by law

items.reveal:
Friede, Busch and Bassen (Journal of Sustainable Finance and Investment, 2015) reviewed 2,200 empirical studies dating back to the 1970s. About 90% reported non-negative ESG-CFP relationships; ~63% reported positive.

Milton Friedman's 1970 New York Times Magazine essay ('The Social Responsibility of Business is to Increase its Profits') argued the opposite. The empirical question turns out to be less stark than either side claims — the effect is usually positive but small, and depends on which ESG element and which industry.
items.why: Strategy debates about CSR are often conducted without reference to the evidence. The aggregate finding is messier than either 'CSR is profitable' or 'CSR is a cost' implies.

items.title: High gearing is risk, not failure
items.claim: A firm has long-term debt of £40 million and equity of £60 million. Its gearing ratio (debt / debt+equity) is 40%. Which statement is most accurate?

options.text: Gearing this high is always dangerous
Higher gearing magnifies returns to shareholders in good times and losses in bad — utilities routinely run 60%+ because cash flows are stable
Equity is always cheaper than debt

items.reveal:
UK water and electricity utilities (Severn Trent, National Grid) often carry gearing above 60% because regulated cash flows make debt servicing predictable. Tech firms (pre-2022) often had near-zero gearing because cash flows were volatile and equity was cheap.

Modigliani and Miller (1958) argued that, in perfect markets, capital structure is irrelevant. In real markets — with taxes, bankruptcy costs and asymmetric information — there is an optimal range. Lehman Brothers' gearing reached above 30:1 (debt:equity) before its 2008 collapse.
items.why: Whether high gearing is reckless depends on what cash flows look like. The number alone tells you little.

items.title: COVID exposed how thin most supply chains were
items.claim: During 2020-22, automotive production was held back by shortages of one component category in particular. Which was it?

options.text: Semiconductors (chips) — the global shortage cost the automotive industry an estimated $210 billion in lost revenue in 2021 alone (AlixPartners)

items.reveal:
When auto demand fell in spring 2020, car makers cancelled chip orders. Foundries (TSMC, Samsung) reallocated capacity to consumer electronics, where demand was surging. When car demand returned, chip capacity was booked out. Ford alone lost around 1.25 million units of production in 2021.

The US CHIPS Act (2022) and EU Chips Act (2023) responded with $50bn+ in subsidies for domestic semiconductor manufacturing — a direct strategic response to the disruption.
items.why: Multi-tier supply chains hide concentration risk. A car maker can have hundreds of direct suppliers but still depend on two or three foundries for chips.
